task.title: A portfolio on GitHub and someone else's repository
task.description:
You are in the folder ~/portfolio on the branch main, and the history has 3 commits. An empty repository https://github.com/anna/portfolio.git has been created on "GitHub", and your classmate Aziz has a repository https://github.com/aziz/notes.git with his Git notes. Write the commands one per line: 1) Connect the remote repository https://github.com/anna/portfolio.git under the name origin and check the list of remote repositories (git remote -v). 2) Send the main branch to GitHub so that origin/main becomes its upstream. 3) Run git status and make sure the branch is up to date with 'origin/main'. 4) Create the branch feature/about and switch to it, create the file about.html with the text

About me

and commit it. 5) Send the feature/about branch to GitHub with the upstream origin/feature/about. 6) Go back to your home folder and clone https://github.com/aziz/notes.git. 7) Go to the folder notes and look at the history (git log --oneline) and the remote repositories. In the end, the history of main on the server matches yours, the server has the branches main and feature/about, both branches have an upstream, and ~/notes holds a copy of Aziz's repository with the whole history.
task.starter_code:
# Write the commands one per line. Lines starting with # are comments. # You are in the folder ~/portfolio on the branch main, and the history has 3 commits. # An empty repository https://github.com/anna/portfolio.git has been created on GitHub # 1. Connect the remote repository under the name origin and check the list of remotes # 2. Send main to GitHub and make origin/main its upstream # 3. Check git status: the branch must be up to date with 'origin/main' # 4. Create the branch feature/about, the file about.html with

About me

, a commit # 5. Send feature/about to GitHub with an upstream # 6. Go back to your home folder and clone https://github.com/aziz/notes.git # 7. Go to notes and look at the history

tests.name: origin with the address of anna/portfolio is connected in ~/portfolio
tests.fail: Connect the remote repository: git remote add origin https://github.com/anna/portfolio.git (the name is origin, the address has no typos). Check it with git remote -v.

tests.name: "GitHub" has exactly two branches: feature/about and main
tests.fail: Send both branches: git push -u origin main and, while on feature/about, git push -u origin feature/about.

tests.name: The history of main on the server matches the local one (all commits, the same hashes)
tests.fail: main on the server must be exactly the same as yours. Don't commit on main after the push, and commit about.html on the branch feature/about.

tests.name: main did not change: 3 original commits, about.html is not in it
tests.check: sim.repo("~/portfolio").log("main").map((c) => c.subject).join("|") === "Add job title|Add styles|Add home page"
tests.fail: The commit with the page about.html must be on the branch feature/about: create it with git switch -c feature/about before the commit.

tests.name: feature/about: one commit with about.html on top of main, the same commit on the server
tests.check:
(() => { const c = sim.repo("~/portfolio").commit("feature/about"); return c !== null && c.parents[0] === sim.repo("~/portfolio").tip("main") && typeof c.files["about.html"] === "string" && c.files["about.html"].includes("

About me

") && sim.remote("https://github.com/anna/portfolio.git").tip("feature/about") !== null && sim.remote("https://github.com/anna/portfolio.git").tip("feature/about") === sim.repo("~/portfolio").tip("feature/about"); })()
tests.fail: feature/about has one commit with the new file about.html (don't forget git add about.html), and it is sent to the server.

tests.name: The upstream of main is origin/main
tests.fail: Send main for the first time with the -u option: git push -u origin main. Without -u, the branch won't remember where to send it.

tests.name: The upstream of feature/about is origin/feature/about
tests.fail: Send the new branch with -u too: git push -u origin feature/about. Just git push answers has no upstream branch.

tests.name: Everything is committed in ~/portfolio
tests.fail: The file about.html must be in a commit on the branch feature/about: git add about.html, then git commit -m.

tests.name: git status after the push showed up to date with 'origin/main'
tests.check: __commands.some((c) => c.cmd.startsWith("git status") && c.out.includes("Your branch is up to date with 'origin/main'"))
tests.fail: Right after git push -u origin main, run git status - Git will report that the branch matches origin/main.

tests.name: The list of remote repositories was checked: git remote -v
tests.fail: After git remote add, look at the result: git remote -v (inside the repository).

tests.name: The repository aziz/notes is cloned into ~/notes: aziz's history and remote origin
tests.check: sim.repo("~/notes") !== null && sim.repo("~/notes").root === "/home/student/notes" && sim.repo("~/notes").remotes().origin === "https://github.com/aziz/notes.git" && JSON.stringify(sim.repo("~/notes").log().map((c) => c.hash)) === JSON.stringify(sim.remote("https://github.com/aziz/notes.git").log("main").map((c) => c.hash)) && sim.repo("~/notes").log().every((c) => c.author === "Aziz Rakhimov")
tests.fail: Go back to your home folder (cd ~) and run git clone https://github.com/aziz/notes.git - the folder ~/notes will appear. Don't clone inside portfolio.

tests.name: The history of the cloned repository was viewed
tests.check: __commands.some((c) => c.cmd.startsWith("git log") && c.out.includes("Add git commands") && c.out.includes("Add README"))
tests.fail: Go to the folder notes (cd notes) and look at the history: git log --oneline.

tests.name: A different local history (5 commits): the server matches it, upstreams are set
tests.check: JSON.stringify(sim.remote("https://github.com/anna/portfolio.git").log("main").map((c) => c.hash)) === JSON.stringify(sim.repo("~/portfolio").log("main").map((c) => c.hash)) && sim.repo("~/portfolio").log("main").length === 5 && sim.remote("https://github.com/anna/portfolio.git").tip("feature/about") !== null && sim.remote("https://github.com/anna/portfolio.git").tip("feature/about") === sim.repo("~/portfolio").tip("feature/about") && sim.repo("~/portfolio").commit("feature/about").parents[0] === sim.repo("~/portfolio").tip("main") && sim.remote("https://github.com/anna/portfolio.git").branches().join(",") === "feature/about,main" && sim.repo("~/portfolio").upstream("main") === "origin/main" && sim.repo("~/portfolio").upstream("feature/about") === "origin/feature/about" && sim.repo("~/notes") !== null && sim.repo("~/notes").root === "/home/student/notes" && sim.repo("~/notes").remotes().origin === "https://github.com/aziz/notes.git" && JSON.stringify(sim.repo("~/notes").log().map((c) => c.hash)) === JSON.stringify(sim.remote("https://github.com/aziz/notes.git").log("main").map((c) => c.hash)) && sim.repo("~/notes").log().every((c) => c.author === "Aziz Rakhimov")
tests.fail: The solution must work for any history: send the main you have and don't create commits on main.

tests.name: The script runs without internal errors
tests.fail: Check the quotes in your echo commands.

hints: To connect the remote repository: git remote add origin https://github.com/anna/portfolio.git. To check: git remote -v.
The first push of a branch is with the -u option: git push -u origin main. Git answers branch 'main' set up to track 'origin/main'.
Create the new branch and switch to it with one command: git switch -c feature/about. Before the commit, the new file needs git add about.html.
Send the branch feature/about with -u too: git push -u origin feature/about. Just git push answers has no upstream branch.
Clone from your home folder, not from the project folder: cd ~, then git clone https://github.com/aziz/notes.git. Git creates the folder notes - go into it (cd notes).

questions.question: What is a remote repository (remote)?
options: A repository that was deleted and can be restored
A copy of the repository on another computer or a server, for example on GitHub
The .git folder on your computer
A separate branch inside your repository
questions.explanation: A remote is the same project history, but in another place: on GitHub, on a company server, on a colleague's computer. Git exchanges commits with it using push, fetch and pull.

questions.question:
What did Git print?

$ git remote -v
origin	https://github.com/anna/portfolio.git (fetch)
origin	https://github.com/anna/portfolio.git (push)
options: Two remote repositories are connected
One remote repository, origin, is connected; you both download from it and send to it
The main branch is sent to GitHub
The repository is cloned
questions.explanation: One origin entry shown twice: the address for downloading (fetch) and for sending (push). Usually they are the same.

questions.question: Type the whole command: send the main branch to origin and make origin/main its upstream (short option).
questions.explanation: -u (--set-upstream) remembers the link main ↔ origin/main. After that, just git push and git pull are enough.

questions.question:
What did Git print?

$ git push
fatal: The current branch feature/about has no upstream branch.
options: The branch feature/about doesn't exist
No remote repository is connected
The branch has never been sent with -u: Git doesn't know where to send it
There is no access to GitHub
questions.explanation: The remote is connected, but the branch has no upstream. Git suggests the fix itself: git push --set-upstream origin feature/about (or git push -u origin feature/about).

questions.question: Match each Git message with its cause.
pairs: git remote add was not run
error: src refspec master does not match any
There is no local branch with this name
A typo in the address or no access to the repository
The account password was typed instead of a token, or the token is wrong
questions.explanation: Read the first line of the error: it almost always names the problem directly.

questions.question: What does origin/main show in your repository?
options: The current state of the main branch on GitHub at this very second
The last state of main on the server known to your Git - as of the last push, fetch or pull
A copy of your local main
A branch you can commit to
questions.explanation: origin/main is a "photo" of the server. It is updated only when you exchange data with the server. If a colleague sent a commit, you will see it in origin/main only after git fetch.

questions.question: What can you use to sign in to GitHub on git push over HTTPS or SSH?
options: A Personal Access Token instead of the password
Your GitHub account password
Git Credential Manager (sign in with a browser)
An SSH key whose public part is added to the GitHub settings
An email without a password
questions.explanation: GitHub hasn't accepted the account password for Git operations since 2021. You need a token, signing in with Git Credential Manager or gh auth login, or an SSH key.

questions.question: How is git fetch different from git pull?
options: They are the same, just synonyms
fetch downloads new commits and updates origin/main but doesn't touch your files; pull = fetch + a merge into the current branch
fetch sends commits, pull downloads them
pull works only with SSH
questions.explanation: fetch is safe: it only "looks at what's new". pull merges the changes into your branch and working directory right away.

questions.question:
What did Git print?

$ git status
On branch main
Your branch is behind 'origin/main' by 1 commit, and can be fast-forwarded.
  (use "git pull" to update your local branch)
options: The server has 1 commit that your main doesn't have; git pull will fast-forward it
You have 1 commit that is not sent yet
The branches have diverged, a conflict is needed
A file is changed but not committed
questions.explanation: behind means "lagging". This message appears after git fetch, when new commits have appeared on the server. ahead would mean the opposite - you have commits that are not sent yet.

questions.question: You already have a local project with commits. You are creating a repository for it on GitHub. What is true?
options: It's better to create the repository empty: without a README, .gitignore or license
You must tick "Add README", otherwise push won't work
After you create it, GitHub shows the address you need for git remote add
A private repository is visible only to you and the people you invite
questions.explanation: If GitHub creates its own first commit with a README, the server and you will have two different histories, and the first push will be rejected. An empty repository accepts your whole history.

questions.question: Match each command with what it does.
pairs: Download the whole repository into a new folder and connect origin
Download new commits, update origin/*, don't touch files
Download and merge into the current branch right away
Send your commits to the server
questions.explanation: clone - once at the start; fetch and pull - get other people's work; push - give your own.

questions.question: Type the whole command: create an SSH key of the modern type ed25519 (without the -C option).
questions.explanation: ssh-keygen creates a pair: the private key ~/.ssh/id_ed25519 (never show it to anyone) and the public ~/.ssh/id_ed25519.pub - you add it to the GitHub settings.
